newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ hires advisors to scope GPS property firm sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ hires advisors to scope GPS property firm sale.

text.p: A New Zealand Treasury official said on Friday that investment bank First NZ Capital and international property agents Jones Lang Wootton (JLW) had been hired to advise the government on its options for the possible privatisation of Government Property Services (GPS).
The official told Reuters the group had been appointed to advise whether the government should sell, if so how, and when.
He said the advisers were to report back to Treasury with their recommendations by the end of August.
Treasurer Winston Peters flagged the prospective sale of GPS in his June budget.
GPS has 35 commercial properties on its books valued at NZ$265.6 million, and shareholders' equity of $173.3 million.
